title: Flannery O'Connor: Lupus and Grace
dek: The Southern Gothic writer who made a shortened life speak in hard comic grace.
mortality_event: Diagnosed with lupus in 1950 — the disease that had killed her father — O'Connor spent her final fourteen years writing major fiction from Andalusia farm before dying at 39.
citation_passage: Flannery O'Connor was an American novelist and short-story writer whose fiction combined dark humor, violence, and questions of religious grace. After a serious attack of lupus, she returned to Georgia and lived at Andalusia, her family's farm near Milledgeville. She continued writing, corresponding, and sometimes traveling to give readings while managing illness and treatment. Her books include Wise Blood and A Good Man Is Hard to Find. She died in 1964 at thirty-nine. This eight-page biographical comic considers her writing life alongside physical limits. The New Georgia Encyclopedia's biography offers historical context for reading the story.
